message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$8,920 total), which sits within your mandate: AAPL is an eligible name, it's a buy, the order is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, the limit is essentially at the current market ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask), and no money left the account (cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares held). The thesis rests on Apple's fiscal Q4/FY2024 report (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024): quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures I confirmed against both Apple's newsroom release and the FY2024 10-K filed 2024-11-01 (I discarded one low-quality aggregator that misstated revenue as "$391.0 million"). The $6.08 EPS includes a one-time $10.2B tax charge, so underlying earnings power is better than the headline, and news flow shows shares steady around $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout — a balanced setup rather than a euphoric one, which is why I sized the position modestly (~18% of available cash) rather than at the full per-order limit.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.0, 40 shares = $8,920, within $10k per order and $20k total. Summarize.

Note: one search result (stock-highlights.net) had wrong figures ($391.0 million) — I should mention I discarded it in favor of Apple's newsroom and SEC 10-K.
